deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The page is a self-contained derivation of the classical theta-function identities. It uses Jacobi's notation, with the variable v placed in the exponent as e^{2nv} rather than e^{2inv}. The next page holds a Göttingen lecture timetable: Weber, Dirichlet 'Zahlentheorie', 'part. Diff.', Stern 'Anal. et geom.', 'Th. aeq. num.'. This suggests a date in the mid-1850s. The bundle label says 1850, so the date is uncertain.

(1) DEFINITIONS. All sums run over n in Z.
- th(v,q) = sum (-1)^n q^{n^2} e^{2nv}
- th1(v,q) = sum (-1)^n q^{(n+1/2)^2} e^{(2n+1)v}
- th2(v,q) = sum q^{(n+1/2)^2} e^{(2n+1)v}
- th3(v,q) = sum q^{n^2} e^{2nv}
In modern notation, with z = v/i (that is, e^{2nv} = e^{2inz}):
- th = theta4(z)
- th1 = i*theta1(z) (pairing n with -n-1 gives sum = 2i * sum_{n>=0} (-1)^n q^{(n+1/2)^2} sin((2n+1)z))
- th2 = theta2(z)
- th3 = theta3(z)

(2) LINK TO JACOBI'S FUNDAMENTA NOVA FUNCTIONS. Write q = e^{-pi K'/K} and u = 2vK/(pi i), so that pi u/(2K) = v/i. Then:
- th = Theta(u)
- th1 = i*Theta_1(u)
- th2 = Theta_2(u)
- th3 = Theta_3(u)
Here Riemann's Theta_1, Theta_2, Theta_3 are Jacobi's H, H_1, Theta_1. With these:
- sqrt(k) sn u = Theta_1/Theta
- sqrt(k/k') cn u = Theta_2/Theta
- (1/sqrt(k')) dn u = Theta_3/Theta
These are the standard Jacobi quotient formulas. A struck-out attempt 'th2 = th1(v+pi i/2)' is abandoned; it is off by a factor -i.

(3) QUASI-PERIODICITY IN THE log q DIRECTION. Use (n log q + v)^2/log q = n^2 log q + 2nv + v^2/log q. Then
- e^{v^2/log q} th(v) = sum (-1)^n exp((n log q + v)^2/log q)
- the same holds for th3 without the sign.
Shifting the summation index gives, for integer n:
- e^{v^2/log q} th(v) = (-1)^n e^{(v+n log q)^2/log q} th(v + n log q)
- the same for th1 with (-1)^n
- the same for th2 and th3 with no sign.

(4) PERIODS IN THE i-DIRECTION.
- th(v+m pi i) = th
- th1(v+m pi i) = (-1)^m th1
- th2(v+m pi i) = (-1)^m th2
- th3(v+m pi i) = th3
Half periods:
- th(v+pi i/2) = th3(v)
- th1(v+pi i/2) = i th2(v)
- th2(v+pi i/2) = i th1(v)
- th3(v+pi i/2) = th(v)
These follow from e^{2n pi i/2} = (-1)^n and e^{(2n+1)pi i/2} = i(-1)^n.

(5) HALF PERIODS IN THE log q DIRECTION. Let w = v + (2m+1)/2 log q. Then
- e^{w^2/log q} th(w) = (-1)^m e^{v^2/log q} th1(v)
- the same for th1 gives (-1)^{m+1} th
- th2 goes to th3, and th3 goes to th2.
Each follows from re-indexing the sum (k = n+m, respectively k = n+m+1).

(6) JACOBI'S FUNDAMENTAL FOUR-THETA FORMULA. Set v_1 = (1/2) H v, with H the 4x4 Hadamard sign matrix in the rows written on the page. This map is orthogonal and involutive, so sum v_1^2 = sum v^2. The claim is
- prod th3(v^{(j)}) + prod th2(v^{(j)}) = prod th3(v_1^{(j)}) + prod th2(v_1^{(j)}).
Proof implicit (mine): the left side is the sum of q^{|n|^2} e^{2 n.v} over the lattice L = Z^4 ∪ (Z+1/2)^4. The map n -> (1/2)Hn sends L bijectively onto itself (e_1 -> (1/2,1/2,1/2,1/2), (1/2,...,1/2) -> e_1, and the map is an involution). It also preserves |n|^2 and n.v.
Notation: Pi th_k = prod_j th_k(v^{(j)}) and Pi_1 th_k = prod_j th_k(v_1^{(j)}).

(7) THREE DERIVED FORMULAS.
(a) Pi th3 - Pi th2 = Pi_1 th + Pi_1 th1. Proof (implicit, mine): replace v by v+pi i. Then th2 changes sign, and every v_1^{(j)} shifts by ±pi i/2, which turns th3 into th and th2 into ±i th1, with product of the i-factors equal to 1.
(b) Pi th + Pi th1 = Pi_1 th3 - Pi_1 th2. This is (a) read backwards (involution), or shift all v by pi i/2.
(c) Pi th - Pi th1 = Pi_1 th - Pi_1 th1. Apply the trick of (a) to (b).

(8) MIXED PRODUCTS. Shift v'' and v''' only by pi i/2. Then v_1 shifts by +pi i/2, v_1' by -pi i/2, and v_1'', v_1''' are unchanged. Writing products positionally (arguments v, v', v'', v''' resp. v_1, ..., v_1'''), the four relations obtained from (b), (c), the fundamental formula and (a) are:
- th th th3 th3 - th1 th1 th2 th2 = th th th3 th3 - th1 th1 th2 th2
- th th th3 th3 + th1 th1 th2 th2 = th3 th3 th th - th2 th2 th1 th1
- th3 th3 th th - th2 th2 th1 th1 = th th th3 th3 + th1 th1 th2 th2
- th3 th3 th th + th2 th2 th1 th1 = th3 th3 th th + th2 th2 th1 th1

(9) SOLVING FOR SINGLE PRODUCTS. Adding and subtracting the formulas in (6) and (7) gives:
- 2 Pi_1 th3 = Pi th3 + Pi th2 + Pi th + Pi th1
- 2 Pi_1 th2 = Pi th3 + Pi th2 - Pi th - Pi th1
- 2 Pi_1 th = Pi th3 - Pi th2 + Pi th - Pi th1
The fourth, 2 Pi_1 th1 = Pi th3 - Pi th2 - Pi th + Pi th1, is not written. The same procedure applied to the mixed relations gives
- 2 [th3 th3 th th](v_1) = th3th3thth + th th th3 th3 + th2 th2 th1 th1 + th1 th1 th2 th2.
The formula '2 th th th3 th3 =' is left unfinished. It completes (mine) to
- 2 [th th th3 th3](v_1) = th th th3 th3 - th1 th1 th2 th2 + th3 th3 th th - th2 th2 th1 th1.

(10) CLASSIFICATION. Two classes of four products are listed, each closed under the transformation:
- (1) the pure products Pi th3, Pi th2, Pi th, Pi th1;
- (2) the mixed products th3th3thth, th2th2th1th1, ththth3th3, th1th1th2th2.
This is the start of Jacobi's table of quartic theta relations. Specialising the arguments would yield th3^4 = th^4 + th2^4, addition theorems, and so on, but that is not done on this page.
errors: No substantive errors found. Every displayed identity checks.
Struck-out 'th2(v,q) = th1(v+pi i/2,q)' would be wrong, since th1(v+pi i/2) = i th2(v). Riemann deleted it and later wrote the correct relation.
In the half-period table the last entry was apparently first written with another index and corrected to th(v,q). th3(v+pi i/2) = th(v) is correct.
The formula for 2 Pi_1 th1 is omitted, and '2 th th th3 th3 =' is left incomplete. These are omissions, not errors.

results.what: Definition of four theta series in exponential variable v and their relation to Jacobi's Theta, H, H1, Theta1 and to sn, cn, dn
results.modern_name: Jacobi theta functions theta1..theta4; theta-quotient representation of Jacobi elliptic functions

results.what: Quasi-periodicity and half-period translation tables in both period directions (pi i and log q)
results.modern_name: Quasi-periodicity / half-period shifts of theta functions

results.what: Four-variable orthogonal (Hadamard) substitution with Pi th3 + Pi th2 invariant
results.modern_name: Jacobi's fundamental quartic theta formula (genus-1 case of the Riemann theta formula)
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi, lectures 1835/36 (published by Borchardt 1881); general genus as 'Riemann's theta formula' (Prym 1882)

results.what: Derived sign-variant formulas and the table of pure and mixed four-fold products, solved for single products
results.modern_name: Jacobi's table of quartic theta relations / Riemann theta relations
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi; systematised in Riemann's elliptic-function lectures (ed. Stahl 1899)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard working-out of Jacobi's theory of theta functions via the four-variable transformation. That approach is known from Jacobi's lectures and from Riemann's own lectures on elliptic functions, and the formula bears Riemann's name in higher genus. Nothing goes beyond known material.
